heading: Compressed files
body:
A release build of the web target (`ty build` or `ty bundle`) writes two compressed copies next to each script, style, page, JSON, SVG, source map and WebAssembly file of 1 KiB or more: `app.js.br` (Brotli) and `app.js.gz` (gzip). The build keeps a copy only when it is smaller than the file. It writes the same bytes every time, and it reuses the copies of files that did not change, so a second build is fast. Native targets get no copies.

`ty start` and `ty preview --static` read the browser's `Accept-Encoding` header and send the Brotli copy, else the gzip copy, else the plain file. A value with `q=0` turns an encoding off. The answer has `Content-Encoding`, `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, and the length and ETag of the copy that is sent, and range and HEAD requests work. The browser unpacks the copy, so pages, services and the service worker get the same bytes as before. While `ty preview` watches your sources, it sends plain files and its builds write no copies, so hot updates stay fast.

On this website the copies make the published files 75% smaller: 11 MB becomes 2.7 MB. The Go module goes from 3.2 MB to 684 KiB, the .NET runtime from 1.5 MB to 461 KiB, the Ruby runtime from 1.1 MB to 347 KiB and the Dart module from 61 KiB to 21 KiB. A CDN or a web server such as nginx (`brotli_static`, `gzip_static`) can send the same copies. `ty build` prints the totals, and ADR 0075 explains the choices.
